answer: A wharf ropewalk gives each agent one rope to keep. The agent twists hemp grown behind the harbor dunes into a single line, crimps a numbered lead tag on it, and hangs it on the wharf crane. Each week a keeper hauls a sandbag on it and logs the tag number and how far it stretches. A second keeper repeats the haul seven days later and cuts any rope that slipped its tag or stretched past the mark. A thousand fake names need a thousand hand-twisted ropes with matching lead tags, and each rope still has to survive its own crane haul before two tides turn.
